experiments.description: Quantum Generative Adversarial Network (QGAN) used to learn a discrete copula distribution from Indian stock index returns, then convert generated binary samples back to copula space and evaluate against bootstrapped real samples.

algorithm.variant: QGAN with quantum generator and quantum MPS discriminator
algorithm.ansatz: Generator circuit ansatz with maximally entangled initial state; RZ, RX, and RZZ gates acting separately on qubits representing each variable; MPS discriminator circuit
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Trained for 1000 epochs; evaluated after adversarial training

hyperparameters.binning_strategy: generic/equal/k-means evaluated; figure example uses k-means

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous copula-space values in [0,1) are discretized into binary strings; for 6 qubits and 2 variables, 3 qubits per variable are concatenated into a 6-bit string.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Learn a target discrete distribution over binary strings corresponding to the copula-transformed data; adversarial objective via maximum likelihood loss.

problem_instance.description: Bivariate copula modeling of Indian stock index returns.

dataset_specification.description: Closing prices from 29-04-2014 to 29-04-2019; returns computed and transformed to copula space using the probability integral transform; 1000 bootstrapped samples used for evaluation.

implementation_details.classical_solver: ndtest for statistical testing; Student T copula as classical baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Returns computed from closing prices; probability integral transform to copula space; discretization via binning strategy.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Generated binary samples converted back to continuous copula space via inverse binning transform; KS and E-statistic computed on generated samples.

speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is inherited from prior theory and not empirically measured here.
